Name: "The Cage"
Summary: When the Enterprise answers a distress call, Capt. Pike encounters manipulative aliens.

Name: "The Man Trap"
Summary: A shape-shifting, salt-craving creature terrorizes the crew of Enterprise.

Name: "Charlie X"
Summary: A powerful teenage boy wreaks havoc aboard the Enterprise.

Name: "Where No Man Has Gone Before"
Summary: While exploring the energy barrier at galaxy's edge that crippled an earlier ship, Kirk's long-time friend and crewmate Gary Mitchell begins mutating into a god-like entity disdainful of the "mortals" around him.

Name: "The Naked Time"
Summary: The Enterprise crew catch a virus that removes their inhibitions.

Name: "The Enemy Within"
Summary: A transporter malfunction creates an evil Kirk.

Name: "Mudd's Women"
Summary: The Enterprise rescues con artist Harry Mudd and his "beautiful" female cargo.

Name: "What Are Little Girls Made Of?"
Summary: Nurse Chapel's long-lost fiancé is found - along with his androids.

Name: "Miri"
Summary: A strange group of children are discovered on an Earth-like planet.

Name: "Dagger of the Mind"
Summary: A new treatment for the criminally insane has deadly results.

Name: "The Corbomite Maneuver"
Summary: While exploring an uncharted area of space, the Enterprise is outmatched and taken in tow by a massive spherical spaceship.

Name: "The Menagerie, Part I"
Summary: Spock fakes a message from the Enterprise's former commander, Christopher Pike, steals the vessel, and sets it on a locked course for the forbidden planet Talos IV.

Name: "The Menagerie, Part II"
Summary: While Spock faces court martial for kidnapping Captain Pike and hijacking the Enterprise, he further explains his actions with mysterious footage about Pike's captivity by the Talosians.

Name: "The Conscience of the King"
Summary: An actor traveling aboard the Enterprise may be a former revolutionary governor who ordered a mass murder twenty years earlier.

Name: "Balance of Terror"
Summary: The Enterprise battles a Romulan ship suspected of destroying outposts near the Neutral Zone.

Name: "Shore Leave"
Summary: The Enterprise crew take shore leave on a planet where their imaginations become reality.

Name: "The Galileo Seven"
Summary: Spock faces difficult command decisions when his shuttle crashes on a hostile world populated by barbarous giants.

Name: "The Squire of Gothos"
Summary: The Enterprise is captured by Trelane, the childish ruler of Gothos.

Name: "Arena"
Summary: Kirk battles an alien captain who has destroyed a Federation outpost.

Name: "Tomorrow is Yesterday"
Summary: The Enterprise is hurled back in time to the year 1969, where the US Air Force sights it as a UFO. The crew must find a way to erase evidence of their visit before trying to get back to their future home.

Name: "Court Martial"
Summary: Kirk is accused of criminal negligence causing the death of one of his subordinates, Lt. Commander Benjamin Finney, and is put on trial for his murder.

Name: "The Return of the Archons"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers a planet where the population act like zombies and obey the will of their unseen ruler, Landru.

Name: "Space Seed"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers an ancient spaceship carrying genetically enhanced supermen from late 20th century Earth and their enigmatic warlord leader: Khan Noonien Singh.

Name: "A Taste of Armageddon"
Summary: On a diplomatic mission, the crew visit a planet that is waging a destructive war fought solely by computer simulation, but the casualties, including the crew of the USS Enterprise, are supposed to be real.

Name: "This Side of Paradise"
Summary: The Enterprise crew finds happiness at a colony where alien spores provide total contentment, at the expense of every negative emotion.

Name: "The Devil in the Dark"
Summary: The Enterprise arrives at Janus VI, where an unknown monster is destroying machinery and killing the miners, threatening the entire mining operation.

Name: "Errand of Mercy"
Summary: Kirk and Spock try to protect the planet Organia from the Klingons, but the natives don't want the Federation's help.

Name: "The Alternative Factor"
Summary: Investigating the cause of a massive, galaxy-wide disruption in space, the Enterprise finds a mad scientist who claims he is being pursued by a hideous being.

Name: "The City on the Edge of Forever"
Summary: Kirk and Spock go back in time to save McCoy – and their own universe.

Name: "Operation -- Annihilate!"
Summary: The Deneva colony is attacked by flying parasites that cause mass insanity while the crew of Enterprise search for a way to stop them.

Name: "Amok Time"
Summary: Spock undergoes the Vulcan mating ceremony.

Name: "Who Mourns for Adonais?"
Summary: The Enterprise is captured by an alien claiming to be Apollo, the Greek god of the sun. He intends to make Carolyn Palamas his queen and the mother of a new race of godlike beings.

Name: "The Changeling"
Summary: The Enterprise finds an ancient interstellar probe from Earth, missing for 265 years, which has somehow mutated into a powerful and intelligent machine sterilizing entire populations that do not meet its standards of perfection.

Name: "Mirror, Mirror"
Summary: A transporter malfunction sends Kirk, McCoy, Scott, and Uhura into a parallel universe where the Federation is replaced by an evil Empire, Kirk is a despot, and Spock is a cunning henchman.

Name: "The Apple"
Writer(s): Max Ehrlich and Gene L. Coon
Summary: The Enterprise crew discovers an Eden-like paradise on Gamma Trianguli VI, controlled by a machine that is revered by the local humanoid primitives as a god.

Name: "The Doomsday Machine"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers a weapon capable of destroying entire planets, and a Starfleet flag officer whose crew was killed by the machine jeopardizes the crew on a crazed mission of revenge.

Name: "Catspaw"
Summary: The Enterprise crew finds witches, a black cat, and a haunted castle on a distant planet.

Name: "I, Mudd"
Summary: A takeover leads Kirk to his old nemesis, Harry Mudd.

Name: "Metamorphosis"
Summary: On an isolated asteroid, Kirk finds Zefram Cochrane, inventor of the warp drive, who has been missing for 150 years.

Name: "Journey to Babel"
Summary: As the Enterprise comes under attack on the way to a diplomatic conference on Babel, one of the alien dignitaries is murdered, and Spock's estranged father Sarek is the prime suspect – but he is also deathly ill, and only Spock can save him.

Name: "Friday's Child"
Summary: The Enterprise becomes involved in a local power struggle on planet Capella IV, where the Klingons want mining rights.

Name: "The Deadly Years"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers a colony full of rapidly ageing scientists. Whatever caused the rapid aging of the scientists soon afflicts the ship's landing party as well. Kirk, Spock, McCoy, and Scott are shocked to discover that they are ageing decades each day and will soon die unless a cure for their condition can be found. The unaffected Chekov may be their only hope for survival.

Name: "Obsession"
Summary: Kirk is determined to hunt down a vampiric entity he failed to destroy in his past.

Name: "Wolf in the Fold"
Summary: Scott is suspected of killing several women while on shore leave on Argelius II. However, a more sinister force may provide a connection between this murder and many previous around the galaxy, including a rampage on ancient Earth.

Name: "The Trouble with Tribbles"
Summary: The Enterprise is overrun by furry creatures while tangling with Klingons and bureaucrats.

Name: "The Gamesters of Triskelion"
Summary: Kirk, Uhura, and Chekov are kidnapped by aliens and forced to fight other aliens so that a mentally superior race can gamble on the winner.

Name: "A Piece of the Action"
Writer(s): David P. Harmon, Gene L. Coon
Summary: Returning to a planet last visited by an Earth ship 100 years earlier, the Enterprise finds a planet that has based its culture on the Chicago gangsters of the 1920s.

Name: "The Immunity Syndrome"
Summary: After Spock senses the destruction of the Vulcan-manned starship Intrepid, the Enterprise encounters an enormous single-celled organism that feeds on energy which threatens the galaxy as it prepares to reproduce.

Name: "A Private Little War"
Summary: On a planet with a primitive civilization, the Enterprise discovers that the Klingons are providing a Stone Age society with increasingly-advanced weaponry.

Name: "Return to Tomorrow"
Summary: Telepathic aliens take over Kirk and Spock's bodies.

Name: "Patterns of Force"
Summary: The Enterprise, searching for a missing Federation historian, discovers that the historian has apparently contaminated the cultural development of the planet where he was assigned as a cultural observer to have it follow the societal path of Nazi Germany in the 1930s and '40s.

Name: "By Any Other Name"
Summary: Extragalactic aliens hijack the Enterprise and turn the crew into inert solids, leaving the four senior officers on their own to exploit their captors' weaknesses.

Name: "The Omega Glory"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers the derelict starship Exeter drifting in space, its entire crew killed by an unknown plague and her captain missing.

Name: "The Ultimate Computer"
Writer(s): Laurence N. Wolfe, D. C. Fontana
Summary: The Enterprise is used to test the new M-5 computer.

Name: "Bread and Circuses"
Summary: Kirk, Spock, and McCoy are captured on a planet that resembles the Roman Empire but with 20th Century technology. They are set to die at the hands of gladiators, for the sake of public spectacle on a TV gameshow.

Name: "Assignment: Earth"
Summary: The Enterprise travels back in time to 1968, where the crew encounters the mysterious Gary Seven who claims to be sent by advanced beings trying to help Earth.

Name: "Spock's Brain"
Summary: An alien woman invades the Enterprise and steals Spock's brain. Kirk, McCoy and a landing party beam down to a planet in a desperate race to retrieve it.

Name: "The Enterprise Incident"
Summary: Acting apparently restless and irrational, Captain Kirk inexplicably orders the Enterprise into Romulan space where the ship is quickly captured by the enemy and Kirk held captive aboard their flagship.

Name: "The Paradise Syndrome"
Summary: Kirk loses his memory and begins a life in a native village.

Name: "And the Children Shall Lead"
Summary: A group of children on the Federation outpost Triacus, under the influence of an evil spirit, commandeer the Enterprise.

Name: "Is There in Truth No Beauty?"
Summary: A beautiful woman escorts an alien ambassador so hideously ugly that the sight of him can drive a Human insane.

Name: "Spectre of the Gun"
Summary: Captain Kirk, Mr. Spock, Dr. McCoy, Scotty, and Chekov are forced to re-enact the gunfight at the O.K. Corral in Tombstone as the team that lost the gunfight

Name: "Day of the Dove"
Summary: An extremely powerful non-corporeal being brings the Enterprise and a Klingon ship in direct conflict with one another.

Name: "For the World is Hollow and I Have Touched the Sky"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers a generational asteroid ship on a collision course with an inhabited planet.

Name: "The Tholian Web"
Summary: While aboard the Starfleet ship USS Defiant, Captain Kirk disappears when the dead ship gets pulled into interspace. The Enterprise is under attack by a mysterious local race, the Tholians.

Name: "Plato's Stepchildren"
Summary: The Enterprise finds a planet inhabited by aliens who were once followers of the Greek philosopher Plato.

Name: "Wink of an Eye"
Summary: The Enterprise is hijacked by hyperaccelerated, sterile aliens who want the crew for breeding stock.

Name: "The Empath"
Summary: On a doomed planet Kirk, Spock, and McCoy become the subjects of an alien experiment whose mysterious intention involves a beautiful, empathic woman.

Name: "Elaan of Troyius"
Summary: The Enterprise transports Elaan, Dohlman of Elas, to an arranged marriage on Troyius.

Name: "Whom Gods Destroy"
Summary: Kirk and Spock are held captive in an insane asylum by a former Starfleet hero.

Name: "Let That Be Your Last Battlefield"
Summary: The crew of the Enterprise find themselves caught in the middle of an intractable conflict with a bizarre fugitive alien and his equally belligerent pursuer.

Name: "The Mark of Gideon"
Summary: Kirk is held captive on an empty duplicate of the USS Enterprise.

Name: "That Which Survives"
Summary: Enterprise crew members are stranded on a ghost planet and terrorized by the image of a beautiful woman.

Name: "The Lights of Zetar"
Summary: At the planetoid Memory Alpha, an Enterprise crew member's body is taken over by mysterious energy lifeforms.

Name: "Requiem for Methuselah"
Summary: While the Enterprise searches for the rare cure to a deadly disease, the landing party is confronted by a reclusive man who is willing to kill to preserve his privacy.

Name: "The Way to Eden"
Summary: The Enterprise picks up a group of renegades who have rejected modern technological life to search for the mythical planet Eden.

Name: "The Cloud Minders"
Writer(s): David Gerrold, Oliver Crawford, Margaret Armen
Summary: Kirk's efforts to obtain a vital mineral are complicated by terrorists striking at the beautiful cloud city Stratos and its virulent apartheid policies.

Name: "The Savage Curtain"
Summary: Kirk and Spock are forced to fight alongside such historical figures as Abraham Lincoln of Earth and Surak of Vulcan by rock-like aliens who want to understand the concepts of "good" and "evil."

Name: "All Our Yesterdays"
Summary: Kirk, Spock, and McCoy are trapped in a planet's distant pasts, where Spock finds love with an exiled woman.

Name: "Turnabout Intruder"
Summary: Dr. Janice Lester, a mad scientist, tries to take control of the Enterprise by switching bodies with Captain Kirk.

Name: "Beyond the Farthest Star"
Summary: The Enterprise finds a deserted starship orbiting a dead star.

Name: "Yesteryear"
Summary: Spock travels back in time to prevent his death as a young Vulcan.

Name: "One of Our Planets Is Missing"
Summary: A mysterious cloud destroys inhabited planets.

Name: "The Lorelei Signal"
Summary: A race of beautiful women remains immortal by stealing the life force of men.

Name: "More Tribbles, More Troubles"
Summary: Cyrano Jones introduces tribbles that cannot reproduce.

Name: "The Survivor"
Summary: The Enterprise finds a long-lost explorer.

Name: "The Infinite Vulcan"
Summary: A mad scientist and a race of intelligent plant life seek to impose peace on the galaxy.

Name: "The Magicks of Megas-Tu"
Summary: At the center of the galaxy, the Enterprise discovers a race of powerful aliens.

Name: "Once Upon a Planet"
Summary: Upon returning to the Amusement Park planet, the Enterprise crew finds that the caretaker has died and the computer has taken over, creating havoc.

Name: "Mudd's Passion"
Summary: The interstellar con artist Harry Mudd returns, selling what he thinks is a fake love potion.

Name: "The Terratin Incident"
Summary: The Enterprise crew begins to shrink after radiation exposure.

Name: "The Time Trap"
Summary: The Enterprise becomes trapped in the Delta Triangle, an area of space where many starships have gone missing. To make matters worse, the ship also has to defend itself from the Klothos, a Klingon vessel commanded by Commander Kor.

Name: "The Ambergris Element"
Summary: The crew of the Enterprise explore a submerged culture on a water world.

Name: "The Slaver Weapon"
Summary: A group of Kzinti divert the shuttle Copernicus and retrieve a newly discovered Slaver weapon.

Name: "The Eye of the Beholder"
Summary: Beaming down to a planet to search for the crew of a missing ship, the crew is captured by its alien inhabitants.

Name: "The Jihad"
Summary: The Vedala, the oldest known spacefaring race, summon Kirk and Spock to recover the Soul of the Skorr, a stolen religious artifact that has the potential to ignite a holy war across the galaxy.

Name: "The Pirates of Orion"
Summary: While Spock lies ill, Orion pirates hijack the drug shipment desperately needed to save his life.

Name: "Bem"
Summary: Ari bn Bem, an erratic observer from the planet Pandro, secretly watches the crew of the USS Enterprise to determine whether the Federation is ready to open diplomatic relations with his advanced species.

Name: "The Practical Joker"
Summary: After passing through a strange space energy cloud, the Enterprise's computer gains an artificial intelligence that is relentlessly bent on making practical jokes on the crew.

Name: "Albatross"
Summary: Following a mission to the planet Dramia, Dr. McCoy is held prisoner, accused of mass genocide caused by a deadly plague committed nineteen years earlier during a previous expedition. When the Enterprise attempts to investigate, it too becomes infected.

Name: "How Sharper Than a Serpent's Tooth"
Summary: The Enterprise encounters a being that once visited the ancient peoples of Earth.

Name: "The Counter-Clock Incident"
Summary: When the Enterprise enters a negative universe, former captain Robert April saves the ship as the crew age backwards.

Name: "Encounter at Farpoint"
Summary: Captain Jean-Luc Picard leads the crew of the USS Enterprise-D on its maiden voyage, to examine a new planetary station for trade with the Federation. On the way, they encounter Q, an omnipotent extra-dimensional being, who challenges Humanity as a barbaric, inferior species. Picard and his new crew must hold off Q's challenge and solve the puzzle of Farpoint station on Deneb IV, a base that is far more than it seems to be.

Name: "The Naked Now"
Writer(s): John D. F. Black,  D. C. Fontana
Summary: The crew of the Enterprise is subjected to an exotic illness that drives them to unusual manic behavior, akin to a type of alcoholic intoxication.

Name: "Code of Honor"
Summary: A mission of mercy is jeopardized when a planetary ruler decides he wants an Enterprise officer as his wife.

Name: "The Last Outpost"
Summary: In pursuit of Ferengi marauders, the Enterprise and its quarry become trapped by a mysterious planet that is draining both ships' energies.

Name: "Where No One Has Gone Before"
Summary: When an experimental engine modification throws the Enterprise to the edge of the known universe, the crew must rely on a mysterious alien to guide the ship home.

Name: "Lonely Among Us"
Summary: While transporting delegates, an alien life form wreaks havoc on the Enterprise computer – and begins to take over the minds of her crew.

Name: "Justice"
Writer(s): John D. F. Black, Worley Thorne
Summary: When Wesley Crusher is condemned to die on an idyllic, primitive planet, Captain Picard must face breaking the Prime Directive to save the boy's life.

Name: "The Battle"
Summary: When a group of Ferengi present Captain Picard with the derelict remains of his old starship, he begins to lose himself in the past.

Name: "Hide And Q"
Summary: Q returns to the Enterprise, testing Commander Riker by giving him the power of the Q.

Name: "Haven"
Summary: Tensions mount as Counselor Troi's arranged marriage nears, and her mother takes a liking to Captain Picard. Meanwhile, a plague ship threatens the planet where they are meeting.

Name: "The Big Goodbye"
Summary: Captain Picard and some of the Enterprise crew get stuck on the holodeck while on their way to an important diplomatic mission.

Name: "Datalore"
Writer(s): Robert Lewin, Maurice Hurley, Gene Roddenberry
Summary: The Enterprise explores Data's home planet, Omicron Theta. They find his brother, and the dark secret he carries.

Name: "Angel One"
Summary: While Riker leads an away team to a female-dominated planet, a mysterious virus spreads among the Enterprise crew.
While a group of technologically advanced aliens board the Enterprise to update the ship's computer systems, Riker discovers just how real a holodeck character can be.

Name: "Too Short A Season"
Summary: An elderly Starfleet admiral hides a deadly secret as he leads the Enterprise-D in a hostage rescue mission.

Name: "When The Bough Breaks"
Summary: Wesley Crusher must protect a group of kidnapped Enterprise-D children while Captain Picard fights for their release.

Name: "Home Soil"
Writer(s): Karl Geurs, Ralph Sanchez, Robert Sabaroff
Summary: When the Enterprise-D visits an outpost in the process of terraforming a dead planet, they find the science team threatened by a mysterious new form of life.

Name: "Coming of Age"
Summary: As Wesley Crusher faces the Starfleet Academy entrance exam on Relva VII, representatives from Starfleet Command conduct an exhaustive investigation into Captain Picard and the Enterprise-D crew.

Name: "Heart of Glory"
Writer(s): Maurice Hurley, Herbert Wright, D. C. Fontana
Summary: Worf's loyalties to Starfleet are tested when three fugitive Klingons come on board the Enterprise-D.

Name: "The Arsenal of Freedom"
Writer(s): Maurice Hurley, Robert Lewin, Richard Manning, Hans Beimler
Summary: Geordi La Forge leads the Enterprise-D into battle while Captain Picard and an away team are trapped on planet Minos, taking fire from a dangerous automated weapons system.

Name: "Symbiosis"
Writer(s): Robert Lewin, Richard Manning, Hans Beimler
Summary: After the Enterprise-D rescues a freighter crew and the ship's important cargo, Captain Picard faces a difficult dilemma: uphold the Prime Directive, or save an entire civilization from exploitation?

Name: "Skin Of Evil"
Summary: A rescue operation to save the lives of a shuttle crew becomes complicated thanks to a malevolent entity, and one Enterprise-D crew member pays the ultimate price in their rescue.

Name: "We'll Always Have Paris"
Writer(s): Deborah Dean Davis, Hannah Louise Shearer
Summary: Captain Picard encounters a woman from his past after her scientist husband's experiments begin to unravel the fabric of time.

Name: "Conspiracy"
Summary: After Captain Picard receives a dark warning from an old friend, the Enterprise-D returns to Earth to stop an alien invasion from taking over Starfleet Command.

Name: "The Neutral Zone"
Writer(s): Deborah McIntyre, Mona Clee, Maurice Hurley
Summary: After rescuing three ancient Humans from cryogenic stasis, the Enterprise-D is ordered to the Romulan Neutral Zone on an important mission.

Name: "The Child"
Writer(s): Jaron Summers, Jon Povill, Maurice Hurley
Summary: Counselor Troi is shocked to find out she is pregnant; Wesley Crusher is weighing his options for the future, with the help of the mysterious proprietor of the ship's lounge, Ten Forward.

Name: "Where Silence Has Lease"
Summary: When an alien traps the Enterprise and threatens to kill half the crew purely out of curiosity, Captain Picard is faced with a grim decision.

Name: "Elementary, Dear Data"
Summary: The Enterprise is threatened when a character in Data and La Forge's holodeck simulation becomes sentient.

Name: "The Outrageous Okona"
Writer(s): Les Menchen, Lance Dickson, David Landsberg, Burton Armus
Summary: The Enterprise crew rescue a "roguish" freighter captain whose ship is malfunctioning, but his presence drags them into an interplanetary feud.

Name: "Loud As A Whisper"
Summary: The Enterprise brings a deaf negotiator to mediate the end of a planetary civil war.

Name: "The Schizoid Man"
Writer(s): Richard Manning, Hans Beimler, Tracy Tormé
Summary: An away team discovers the dying Doctor Ira Graves, who claims to be Data's "grandfather."

Name: "Unnatural Selection"
Summary: The Enterprise investigates the deaths of the crew of the USS Lantree, who all died of old age.

Name: "A Matter Of Honor"
Writer(s): Wanda M. Haight, Gregory Amos, Burton Armus
Summary: Riker serves as an exchange officer on a Klingon warship.

Name: "The Measure Of A Man"
Summary: Picard must prove Data is legally a sentient being with rights and freedoms under Federation law when transfer orders demand Data's reassignment for study and disassembly.

Name: "The Dauphin"
Summary: Wesley falls in love with the new leader of a war-torn planet.

Name: "Contagion"
Summary: The Enterprise and a Romulan warbird are attacked by the same computer virus that has already destroyed one Federation starship of the same class as the Enterprise.

Name: "The Royale"
Summary: The Enterprise investigates the wreckage of a 21st century Earth spaceship orbiting a distant planet and the appearance of a casino with inhabitants based on a rather poorly written paperback novel.

Name: "Time Squared"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers a duplicate of Picard from six hours in the future.

Name: "The Icarus Factor"
Summary: When Commander Riker is offered command of the starship Aries, his estranged father, Kyle Riker, is sent by Starfleet to brief him on the mission. Meanwhile, Data, La Forge, Dr. Pulaski, Wesley, and O'Brien help Worf celebrate the anniversary of his Rite of Ascension.

Name: "Pen Pals"
Writer(s): Hannah Louise Shearer, Melinda M. Snodgrass
Summary: Data makes contact with a young girl from a pre-warp civilization on a planet facing imminent annihilation. The Enterprise must wrestle with the moral dilemma of violating the Prime Directive or standing by while Data's friend dies.

Name: "Q Who"
Summary: Q throws the Enterprise into uncharted space where it encounters and is engaged by a dangerous alien vessel of a previously unknown species: the Borg. When the vessel instantly and effortlessly overwhelms the Enterprise, Picard realizes that the Federation may not be as ready for the future as he thought.

Name: "Samaritan Snare"
Summary: Picard must undergo a serious medical procedure while the Enterprise-D deals with a Pakled ship, which lures the Enterprise away in hopes of stealing its technology.

Name: "Up The Long Ladder"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers two threatened colonies which must cooperate to survive.

Name: "Manhunt"
Summary: Lwaxana Troi arrives on the Enterprise, intent on finding a husband.

Name: "The Emissary"
Writer(s): Richard Manning, Hans Beimler, Thomas H. Calder
Summary: The Enterprise crew has to deal with a Klingon sleeper ship whose occupants don't know the Federation and Klingons are at peace. On-board to help them is an emissary, who (coincidentally) is one of Worf's former love interests.

Name: "Peak Performance"
Summary: With the Borg threat in mind, Starfleet stages a war-game simulation pitting Captain Picard and the Enterprise against Commander Riker and the eighty-year-old starship Hathaway. However, when the Ferengi suddenly attack, the Enterprise is crippled, forcing Picard into a seemingly no-win situation.

Name: "Shades of Gray"
Writer(s): Maurice Hurley, Richard Manning, Hans Beimler
Summary: Commander Riker fights for his life in sickbay after he is infected by an alien parasite while on an away mission. Dr. Pulaski soon discovers that the only way to save Riker's life is to force his mind to relive painful memories.

Name: "Evolution"
Summary: An obsessed scientist arrives on the Enterprise to perform a once-in-a-lifetime experiment. Accidentally released nanites, however, threaten both it and the ship.

Name: "The Ensigns of Command"
Summary: Data must convince a colony of 15,000 people to evacuate before the aliens who own the planet arrive.

Name: "The Survivors"
Summary: The Enterprise investigates two survivors living on the only undamaged patch of land on a devastated planet.

Name: "Who Watches The Watchers"
Summary: The Enterprise must undo the damage when a primitive civilization discovers a Federation observation team and concludes that the Starfleet personnel are gods.

Name: "The Bonding"
Summary: Worf decides to take into his House the child of a slain subordinate, but the child is having trouble accepting his mother's death, especially when she mysteriously reappear

Name: "Booby Trap"
Writer(s): Michael Wagner, Ron Roman, Michael Piller, Richard Danus
Summary: While investigating a 1,000-year-old alien derelict, the Enterprise gets caught in the same energy trap which doomed that vessel a millennium ago.

Name: "The Enemy"
Summary: La Forge and a Romulan are trapped on a planet ravaged by electromagnetic storms; Worf turns out to be the only viable donor to save the life of an injured Romulan aboard the Enterprise.

Name: "The Price"
Summary: The Enterprise hosts negotiations for possession of the only known stable wormhole.

Name: "The Vengeance Factor"
Summary: The Enterprise tries to negotiate an end to raids launched by a group called the "Gatherers," but a murder threatens to prevent peace.

Name: "The Defector"
Summary: The Enterprise grants asylum to a defector from the Romulan Empire, who claims to have vital information concerning a renewed Romulan offensive against the Federation.

Name: "The Hunted"
Summary: While the Enterprise-D is reviewing a seemingly idyllic planet's application for Federation membership, an escaped prisoner leads her crew to discover an ugly secret: the government's shameful treatment of its war veterans.

Name: "The High Ground"
Summary: Doctor Crusher is captured by terrorists who want to involve the Federation in their struggle for freedom.

Name: "Deja Q"
Summary: Q is seeking asylum on the Enterprise after he has been thrown out of the Continuum and stripped of his powers.

Name: "A Matter of Perspective"
Summary: When Riker is charged with the murder of a prominent scientist, each side uses the holodeck to show their side of the story.

Name: "Yesterday's Enterprise"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Richard Manning, Hans Beimler, Ronald D. Moore, Trent Christopher Ganino, Eric A. Stillwell
Summary: While investigating a temporal rift, the Enterprise encounters a ghost from its own past – the USS Enterprise-C, which travels twenty two years into the future and changes the course of history. With the flow of history changed, Tasha Yar still lives and the Federation is losing a decades-long war with the Klingon Empire.

Name: "The Offspring"
Summary: Data successfully creates a new android, which he views as his child. However, the magnitude of his accomplishment quickly attracts the scrutiny of Starfleet, who wants to separate the child from Data and the Enterprise for study. Matters are complicated further when the child begins to develop beyond Data's abilities.

Name: "Sins of The Father"
Writer(s): Drew Deighan, Ronald D. Moore, W. Reed Moran
Summary: Worf is plunged head-first into the politics of the Klingon Empire when his deceased father is accused of treason.

Name: "Allegiance"
Summary: Captain Picard and three other people are abducted and imprisoned by an unknown force and replaced by duplicates.

Name: "Captain's Holiday"
Summary: Picard takes a much-needed vacation on Risa, but unwelcome events keep interfering with his rest.

Name: "Tin Man"
Summary: The Enterprise races against Romulans to make first contact with a powerful entity code-named "Tin Man."

Name: "Hollow Pursuits"
Summary: Lieutenant Barclay, an introverted diagnostic engineer, is having difficulties dealing with his fantasies.

Name: "The Most Toys"
Summary: A trader fakes Data's death to add him to his collection of rare and unique objects.

Name: "Sarek"
Summary: Violent emotions sweep the Enterprise when Ambassador Sarek, a foundational figure of the Federation, comes aboard to conclude a decades-long diplomatic mission.

Name: "Ménage à Troi"
Summary: A Ferengi DaiMon kidnaps Riker, Deanna, and Lwaxana Troi.

Name: "Transfigurations"
Summary: The Enterprise rescues a critically injured amnesiac who is undergoing a mysterious transformation.

Name: "The Best of Both Worlds"
Summary: The Borg begin an invasion of Federation space much sooner than was expected. With the Enterprise unable to affect them, the Borg capture Captain Picard and turn him into one of their own.

Name: "The Best of Both Worlds, Part II"
Summary: With Captain Picard assimilated by the Borg, the enemy is able to totally obliterate a Starfleet armada at Wolf 359, leaving Riker in command of the Enterprise and forced to go one on one with his former captain.

Name: "Family"
Summary: Captain Picard takes leave on Earth and visits his family while recovering from his assimilation into the Borg. Worf's Human parents visit Enterprise and help him deal with his discommendation.

Name: "Brothers"
Summary: Data jeopardizes an emergency mission to save an ill child when he receives a signal from his creator, Noonien Soong.

Name: "Suddenly Human"
Writer(s): Ralph Phillips, John Whelpley, Jeri Taylor
Summary: The Enterprise crew discovers a young Human boy being raised by the aliens who killed his parents.

Name: "Remember Me"
Summary: Following an anomaly in a warp bubble experiment, Dr. Crusher finds that crewmembers are beginning to disappear, while she is the only one who seems to notice.

Name: "Legacy"
Summary: The survivors from a doomed freighter crash-land on Turkana IV, Tasha Yar's homeworld, and are taken hostage by a dissident faction. When the Enterprise moves to intervene, they are joined by Tasha's sister Ishara who has ulterior motives.

Name: "Reunion"
Writer(s): Drew Deighan, Thomas Perry, Jo Perry, Ronald D. Moore, Brannon Braga
Summary: Captain Picard is selected to arbitrate the selection of a new Chancellor for the Klingon Empire and, in doing so, find out who dishonorably murdered the old Chancellor. Also involved is Ambassador K'Ehleyr, who has a surprise for Worf: their son.

Name: "Future Imperfect"
Writer(s): J. Larry Carroll, David Bennett Carren
Summary: After an away mission to Alpha Onias III interrupts Commander Riker's birthday party, the first officer suddenly awakens in sick-bay sixteen years in the future where he is the captain of the Enterprise and about to negotiate a peace treaty with the Romulan Star Empire.

Name: "Final Mission"
Summary: On his way to Starfleet Academy, Wesley Crusher must care for an injured Captain Picard after their shuttle crashes on a desert moon.

Name: "The Loss"
Writer(s): Hilary J. Bader, Allan J. Adler, Vanessa Greene
Summary: Counselor Troi loses her empathic powers; the Enterprise is slowly pulled off course by an unknown force existing in two-dimensional form into a deadly cosmic string.

Name: "Data's Day"
Summary: Data records a day in his life for Commander Bruce Maddox, including observations on Chief O'Brien's wedding, and the mystery of a Vulcan ambassador who apparently dies in a transporter accident.

Name: "The Wounded"
Writer(s): Stuart Charno, Sara Charno,  Cy Chermak, Jeri Taylor
Summary: When Captain Benjamin Maxwell apparently goes rogue, the Enterprise is ordered to apprehend him before his actions result in another war between the Federation and the Cardassian Union.

Name: "Devil's Due"
Summary: The USS Enterprise-D responds to a distress signal from a science station on Ventax II, where the planet is in chaos over the return of a being who claims to be that culture's "devil".

Name: "Clues"
Summary: The crew of the Enterprise wakes up after apparently passing through a wormhole, finding mysteries surrounding their blackout. Data begins to act suspiciously, prompting the command staff to wonder if he has been compromised.

Name: "First Contact"
Writer(s): Dennis Bailey, David Bischoff, Joe Menosky, Ronald D. Moore, Michael Piller, Marc Scott Zicree
Summary: An injury to Commander Riker during a reconnaissance mission threatens the prospects for first contact with a culture on the verge of warp travel.

Name: "Galaxy's Child"
Summary: La Forge finds out that a scientist is hardly what he imagined her to be. Meanwhile, they must work together to save the child of a space-borne alien the Enterprise has accidentally killed.

Name: "Night Terrors"
Writer(s): Shari Goodhartz, Pamela Douglas, Jeri Taylor
Summary: The Enterprise crew is affected when they are adrift in a remote area of space, and find themselves unable to dream.

Name: "Identity Crisis"
Summary: Something is luring a former away team back to the planet they once investigated five years ago – an away team that La Forge was a part of.

Name: "The Nth Degree"
Summary: After an encounter with a mysterious alien probe, Lieutenant Barclay begins to exhibit signs of profound intelligence, ultimately hooking himself into the ship's computer and hurling the Enterprise into apparent danger.

Name: "Qpid"
Summary: Q picks up on romantic tensions between Captain Picard and an old flame, transporting them and the senior officers into a representation of Robin Hood.

Name: "The Drumhead"
Summary: After an encounter with a mysterious alien probe, Lieutenant Barclay begins to exhibit signs of profound intelligence, ultimately hooking himself into the ship's computer and hurling the Enterprise into apparent danger.

Name: "Half a Life"
Summary: Lwaxana Troi causes trouble when she finds out that a scientist she has fallen in love with is due to commit ritual suicide.

Name: "The Host"
Summary: A Trill ambassador is on board to mediate a dispute, and falls in love with Dr. Crusher. When the Trill host is killed, the symbiont has to be temporarily joined to Commander Riker to continue the negotiations – and the affair.

Name: "The Mind's Eye"
Summary: En route to Risa, Geordi La Forge is taken prisoner on a Romulan ship and mentally conditioned to assassinate a Klingon governor in order to implicate the Federation as enemies of the Empire and unbalance relations between the two governments.

Name: "In Theory"
Summary: In his latest attempt to understand Humanity, Data accepts the affections of Jenna D'Sora and pursues a romantic relationship with her. In the meantime, a nebula the Enterprise is passing through is causing strange things to happen on the ship.

Name: "Redemption"
Summary: Picard balances his Federation and Klingon duties as new Klingon Chancellor Gowron faces a civil war. Worf and his brother Kurn fight to regain their father's honor.

Name: "Redemption II"
Summary: As the House of Duras is nearing victory over Worf and the forces of Gowron, Starfleet, led by Picard, works to expose Romulan interference in the Klingon Civil War.

Name: "Darmok"
Summary: Picard is captured, then trapped on a planet with an alien captain who speaks a metaphorical language incompatible with the universal translator. They must learn to communicate with each other before a deadly planetary beast overwhelms them.

Name: "Ensign Ro"
Summary: The Enterprise takes on Ensign Ro Laren to help track down Bajoran terrorists who attacked a Federation colony.

Name: "Silicon Avatar"
Summary: The Enterprise gives chase to the Crystalline Entity after it destroys a Federation colony. A xenologist, who has a motivation all her own with respect to the Crystalline Entity, is assigned to the Enterprise to assist in the investigations.

Name: "Disaster"
Writer(s): Ron Jarvis, Philip A. Scorza, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: A quantum filament disables the Enterprise, leaving Counselor Troi in command on the bridge, and various groups on different parts of the ship facing perils alone.

Name: "The Game"
Writer(s): Susan Sackett, Fred Bronson, Brannon Braga
Summary: Wesley Crusher visits the Enterprise only to see everyone behaving strangely on account of an addictive, mind-controlling game.

Name: "Unification I"
Writer(s): Rick Berman, Michael Piller, Jeri Taylor
Summary: To the Federation's surprise, Ambassador Spock has traveled to Romulus. Fearing he has defected, they send Captain Picard and Data on a covert mission to determine why.

Name: "Unification II"
Summary: On Romulus, Picard and Data meet with Spock, who claims to be trying to reunite the Romulans and Vulcans. While Spock works to achieve his goal, powers within the Romulan government seek to pervert his mission into an invasion of the Federation.

Name: "A Matter Of Time"
Summary: A time traveler claiming to be from the 26th century arrives to witness an attempt to save a doomed planet.

Name: "New Ground"
Writer(s): Sara Charno, Stuart Charno, Grant Rosenberg
Summary: Worf's son Alexander comes to live on the Enterprise; the crew helps guide a test vehicle for a revolutionary new form of interstellar travel.

Name: "Hero Worship"
Summary: Data helps the only survivor of a wrecked ship, a child, cope with the loss of his parents. Meanwhile, the crew investigates the cause of the wreck.

Name: "Violations"
Writer(s): Shari Goodhartz, T. Michael, Pamela Gray, Jeri Taylor
Summary: Several crew members suffer violent hallucinations and comas as alien researchers visit the ship.

Name: "The Masterpiece Society"
Writer(s): James Kahn, Adam Belanoff, Michael Piller
Summary: The Enterprise tries to save a "perfect" colony from destruction, but the assistance causes damage of its own.

Name: "Conundrum"
Summary: After the crew's memories are mysteriously erased, the computer records indicate that the Federation is at war with the Lysians, and that the Enterprise has been ordered to attack their command center.

Name: "Power Play"
Writer(s): Paul Ruben, Maurice Hurley, René Balcer, Herbert Wright, Brannon Braga
Summary: Alien entities take over the minds of Data, Troi, and Miles O'Brien.

Name: "Ethics"
Writer(s): Sara Charno, Stuart Charno, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: After Worf is paralyzed by a freak accident, his only hope may be a visiting doctor with questionable medical ethics.

Name: "The Outcast"
Summary: Riker falls in love with Soren, a member of an androgynous race known as the J'naii, who dares to be female.

Name: "Cause And Effect"
Summary: The destruction of the Enterprise near a distortion in the space-time continuum causes a temporal causality loop to form, trapping the ship and crew in time and forcing them to relive the events that led to their deaths.

Name: "The First Duty"
Summary: Following an accident during an Academy training exercise that leads to the death of one of his friends, Wesley Crusher must decide whether loyalty or truth is the first duty.

Name: "Cost Of Living"
Summary: Lwaxana Troi is on board the Enterprise-D to hold her wedding ceremony, and she also takes an interest in Worf's son Alexander, encouraging him to adopt her carefree ways.

Name: "The Perfect Mate"
Writer(s): René Echevarria, Gary Perconte, Michael Piller
Summary: Picard serves as host for a peace treaty between two warring planets, but he may be unable to resist the reconciliation "gift" – a beautiful empathic metamorph who is to be presented by one leader as the other's wife.

Name: "Imaginary Friend"
Writer(s): Jean Louise Matthias, Ronald Wilkerson, Richard Fliegel, Edithe Swensen, Brannon Braga
Summary: As the Enterprise explores a nebula, a little girl's imaginary friend becomes terrifyingly real.

Name: "I Borg"
Summary: The discovery of an injured adolescent Borg brings to the surface hard feelings for both Captain Picard and Guinan for what the Borg Collective had done to them. Matters are complicated when plans to use the young Borg to destroy his people are halted when it is discovered that the Borg has become an individual.

Name: "The Next Phase"
Summary: Geordi La Forge and Ensign Ro are believed dead after a transporter malfunction. However, they soon discover that their state may not actually be "death".

Name: "The Inner Light"
Summary: An alien probe controls and disables Captain Picard, who wakes up as "Kamin," a resident of the planet Kataan. While the crew of the Enterprise tries to jar the probe's influence, "Kamin" lives through the final, dying decades of his homeworld in the span of approximately twenty minutes in the form of an interactive "ancestor simulation".

Name: "Time's Arrow"
Summary: An engineering team finds evidence of an alien presence on Earth in 19th century San Francisco: Data's severed head, buried five hundred years ago.

Name: "Time's Arrow, Part II"
Summary: Trapped in 19th century San Francisco, the crew of the Enterprise must locate Data and prevent his death while stopping the Devidians from destroying Earth's history.

Name: "Realm Of Fear"
Summary: Lieutenant Barclay faces his fear of transporting, but now he thinks that he's being attacked by a creature inside the transporter beam.

Name: "Man Of The People"
Summary: As an ambassador mediates peace talks to end a fierce civil war, Deanna Troi begins to act erratically after spending some time with him.

Name: "Relics"
Summary: The Enterprise discovers a ship that crashed on a Dyson sphere more than seventy-five years prior with a single survivor suspended in the transporter buffer: Captain Montgomery Scott.

Name: "Schisms"
Writer(s): Jean Louise Matthias, Ronald Wilkerson, Brannon Braga
Summary: Enterprise crew members report that they go to sleep but wake up exhausted; a mysterious subspace pocket forms inside a cargo bay.

Name: "True Q"
Summary: Q once again graces the Enterprise with a visit, claiming that a young intern aboard is really a Q.

Name: "Rascals"
Writer(s): Ward Botsford, Diana Dru Botsford, Michael Piller, Allison Hock
Summary: Captain Picard, Ensign Ro, Guinan, and Keiko O'Brien are regressed physiologically to the age of twelve, by a transporter accident, but retain their adult memories, resulting in different reactions from each. When rogue Ferengi hijack the Enterprise, the young crewmembers, along with Alexander Rozhenko, lead the revolt.

Name: "A Fistful of Datas"
Summary: After a computer malfunction, Worf, his son Alexander Rozhenko, and Counselor Deanna Troi are trapped in an Old West holodeck program wherein the interactive characters physically resemble and have the same enhanced abilities as Data.

Name: "The Quality of Life"
Summary: Data discovers a group of robots that he believes qualify as lifeforms.

Name: "Chain Of Command, Part I"
Summary: Picard, Worf, and Dr. Crusher are reassigned from the Enterprise to a secret mission. Meanwhile, the Enterprise is under the command of Captain Edward Jellico, who immediately starts making changes, much to the dismay of the crew.

Name: "Chain Of Command, Part II"
Summary: Captain Picard's secret mission fails, leading to him being captured by Cardassians. As he is tortured by his captors, Captain Jellico and the Enterprise attempt to prevent war with the Cardassian Union.

Name: "Ship In A Bottle"
Summary: Professor Moriarty returns, only this time he gains control of the Enterprise in his quest to leave the holodeck.

Name: "Aquiel"
Writer(s): Jeri Taylor, Brannon Braga, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: Geordi La Forge falls in love with a woman accused of murder in an isolated communication relay station. The Enterprise crew investigates the crime; the only other suspect is a Klingon officer who frequently visited the station.

Name: "Face Of The Enemy"
Summary: Troi is captured and forced to masquerade as a Romulan intelligence officer in a plot to aid the defection of several high-ranking Romulan officials.

Name: "Tapestry"
Summary: After being attacked on an away mission, Picard dies and meets Q in the afterlife who offers him the chance to change a crucial moment in his history and prevent the mistakes he made in his youth.

Name: "Birthright, Part I"
Summary: At Deep Space 9, Worf investigates reports that his father is still alive and an engineering accident causes Data to experience a vision of his father, Dr. Soong.

Name: "Birthright, Part II"
Summary: In the Romulan prison camp, Worf teaches the Klingon children about their culture.

Name: "Starship Mine"
Summary: On an evacuated USS Enterprise-D, Picard plays a deadly game of cat-and-mouse with terrorists who want to steal explosive toxic waste from the warp core as a lethal beam sweeps the ship.

Name: "Lessons"
Summary: Picard falls in love with one of his subordinates, but he can't deal with having to order her into dangerous situations.

Name: "The Chase"
Summary: Picard tries to finish his old archaeology teacher's monumental last mission: solving a puzzle that leads Humans, Romulans, Klingons and Cardassians to the secret of life in this galaxy, revealing the origin of humanoid life.

Name: "Frame of Mind"
Summary: Riker thinks he is losing his mind when reality keeps shifting between an alien hospital and the Enterprise, where he is rehearsing a play.

Name: "Suspicions"
Summary: Dr. Crusher violates Starfleet regulations and medical ethics when she investigates the death of a Ferengi scientist.

Name: "Rightful Heir"
Writer(s): James E. Brooks, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: At the Klingon monastery on Boreth, Worf sees a very real vision of Kahless the Unforgettable.

Name: "Second Chances"
Summary: The Enterprise finds a second Will Riker on a planet that he helped evacuate eight years ago.

Name: "Timescape"
Summary: Aboard a runabout, Picard, Data, La Forge, and Troi encounter time distortions; they also discover the Enterprise, frozen in time while in battle with a Romulan warbird – and seconds away from destruction.

Name: "Descent"
Summary: The Borg begin a new offensive against the Federation, but this time they're acting as individuals; Data experiences his first emotions while fighting them.

Name: "Descent, Part II"
Summary: Picard tries to free Data from Lore's control; the Enterprise battles the Borg ship.

Name: "Liaisons"
Writer(s): Roger Eschbacher, Jaq Greenspon, Jeanne Carrigan-Fauci, Lisa Rich
Summary: As alien dignitaries visit the ship, Picard's shuttle crashes on a desolate planet where he meets a woman who has been stranded there for seven years.

Name: "Interface"
Summary: La Forge uses a virtual reality probe to explore a wrecked ship inside a gas giant, but he's preoccupied by the disappearance of his mother's ship.

Name: "Gambit, Part I"
Summary: While investigating Picard's apparent death, Riker is captured by pirates pillaging Romulan archaeological sites.

Name: "Gambit, Part II"
Summary: Picard and Riker try to find out what the pirates want while the Enterprise pursues them.

Name: "Phantasms"
Summary: The crew helps Data investigate when his dream program suddenly begins generating nightmares which make him act strangely. Meanwhile, Captain Picard attempts to avoid attending a boring Starfleet banquet.

Name: "Dark Page"
Summary: Lwaxana Troi visits the Enterprise, but she's preoccupied by a dark secret that she has carried for years.

Name: "Attached"
Summary: After escaping imprisonment on an alien world, Picard and Dr. Crusher find that their thoughts are connected by brain implants.

Name: "Force of Nature"
Summary: Investigating the disappearance of several ships, the Enterprise discovers two scientists who claim that warp drive is destructive to the fabric of subspace.

Name: "Inheritance"
Summary: Data meets Juliana Tainer, former wife of Dr. Noonien Soong and Data's "mother," but she holds a shocking secret that even she doesn't know she carries.

Name: "Parallels"
Summary: After Worf returns from a bat'leth tournament, he is the only person who notices subtle changes on the Enterprise.

Name: "The Pegasus"
Summary: When Riker's first commanding officer comes aboard to aid in the search for the vessel they served on, he is forced to rethink the actions he took at that time.

Name: "Homeward"
Summary: Worf's foster brother violates the Prime Directive by saving a group of villagers from a doomed planet.

Name: "Sub Rosa"
Summary: Beverly Crusher attends her grandmother's funeral, but a mysterious entity that inhabited her grandmother is now focusing on her.

Name: "Lower Decks"
Writer(s): Ronald Wilkerson, Jean Louise Matthias, René Echevarria
Summary: Junior officers speculate on the reasons for recent unusual actions taken by the command crew near the Cardassian border.

Name: "Thine Own Self"
Summary: Data suffers amnesia in a primitive society while Troi applies for a promotion.

Name: "Masks"
Summary: While investigating a rogue comet, the cultural archive concealed inside begins taking over both the Enterprise and Data.

Name: "Eye of the Beholder"
Summary: Counselor Troi's investigation into the suicide of a crewman suggests a murder was committed aboard the Enterprise while it was being built, and that the murderer is still aboard.

Name: "Genesis"
Summary: Enterprise crew members de-evolve into prehistoric creatures after a medical treatment by Dr. Crusher goes wrong.

Name: "Journey's End"
Summary: As a result of a long-disputed treaty with the Cardassians, the Federation has agreed to return several planets to Cardassian control. One such planet, Dorvan V, is inhabited by the descendants of Native Americans. They do not wish to leave their new home, which they had spent many years searching for.

Name: "Firstborn"
Summary: A mysterious family friend and advisor encourages Worf's son Alexander to become a warrior.

Name: "Bloodlines"
Summary: DaiMon Bok threatens the life of a son Picard never knew he had.

Name: "Emergence"
Summary: A series of puzzling events on and off the holodeck lead the crew of the Enterprise to a surprising conclusion: The ship is creating its own offspring. The crew has to assist with this arduous process to ensure the survival of the emerging lifeform – and their own.

Name: "Preemptive Strike"
Summary: Lieutenant Ro is sent undercover to root out a Maquis cell.

Name: "All Good Things..."
Summary: Picard learns from Q that he is to be the cause of the annihilation of Humanity and begins an incredible journey through time from the present, to the past when he first took command of the Enterprise, to twenty-five years into the future.

Name: "Emissary"
Summary: Three years after his wife died at the hands of the Borg and following the Cardassian withdrawal from the planet Bajor, Commander Benjamin Sisko and a new crew of Starfleet and Bajoran officers take command of an abandoned Cardassian space station and make an incredible discovery that will change the galaxy and Sisko's future.

Name: "Past Prologue"
Summary: A Bajoran terrorist tests Kira's loyalties to the Federation when he attempts to rid Bajor of the Federation for good.

Name: "A Man Alone"
Summary: An old enemy of Odo's is murdered behind locked doors, and all the evidence points to Odo as the killer.

Name: "Babel"
Writer(s): Sally Caves, Ira Steven Behr, Michael McGreevey, Naren Shankar
Summary: A virus infects the station's residents, making almost everyone unable to speak coherently.

Name: "Captive Pursuit"
Summary: O'Brien helps an alien from the Gamma Quadrant as hunters descend on the station searching for their humanoid prey.

Name: "Q-Less"
Writer(s): Hannah Louise Shearer, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Archaeologist Vash arrives from the Gamma Quadrant as Q plagues the station and an unknown force threatens to destroy it.

Name: "Dax"
Writer(s): D. C. Fontana, Peter Allan Fields
Summary: New evidence reopens a thirty-year-old murder case and Dax's previous host, Curzon, is the prime suspect.

Name: "The Passenger"
Writer(s): Morgan Gendel, Robert Hewitt Wolfe, Michael Piller
Summary: An alien criminal, attempting to prolong his life, hides his consciousness inside the mind of a station crew member.

Name: "Move Along Home"
Writer(s): Michael Piller, Frederick Rappaport, Lisa Rich, Jeanne Carrigan-Fauci
Summary: A visiting delegation from the Gamma Quadrant turns four crew members into "pieces" for a bizarre game.

Name: "The Nagus"
Summary: With the sudden death of Grand Nagus Zek, Quark becomes the new leader of the Ferengi Alliance, but he also becomes a target for murder.

Name: "Vortex"
Summary: A fugitive from the Gamma Quadrant attempts to trade evidence about Odo's people for freedom.

Name: "Battle Lines"
Writer(s): Hilary J. Bader, Richard Danus, Evan Carlos Somers
Summary: A runabout carrying Kai Opaka crashes on a planet of eternal war, where it is impossible for the combatants to die.

Name: "The Storyteller"
Writer(s): Kurt Michael Bensmiller, Ira Steven Behr
Summary: Chief O'Brien is appointed spiritual leader of a Bajoran village. Meanwhile, Nog and Jake try to help their new friend settle a struggle between two Bajoran villages.

Name: "Progress"
Summary: Kira leads the evacuation of a Bajoran moon which is being converted into a massive power plant that will render the entire surface uninhabitable, but an old farmer refuses to leave. Back on the station, Jake and Nog set out to turn an inordinate amount of seemingly worthless condiments into profit.

Name: "If Wishes Were Horses"
Writer(s): Nell McCue Crawford, William L. Crawford, Michael Piller
Summary: Station residents suddenly find their imaginations are manifested in physical form; a spatial rift threatens to destroy the Bajoran system.

Name: "The Forsaken"
Writer(s): Jim Trombetta, Don Carlos Dunaway, Michael Piller
Summary: An alien computer program wreaks havoc with the station's systems during a visit from Lwaxana Troi and other ambassadors.

Name: "Dramatis Personae"
Summary: The crew becomes infected by a telepathic imprint of a culture that destroyed itself.

Name: "Duet"
Writer(s): Lisa Rich, Jeanne Carrigan-Fauci, Peter Allan Fields
Summary: After a Cardassian man arrives on the station suffering from an illness that he could only have contracted at a Bajoran labor camp during the Occupation, Major Kira leads an investigation to determine whether he is actually a notorious war criminal.

Name: "In the Hands of the Prophets"
Summary: Orthodox Bajorans object to secular teachings about the wormhole in the station's school, causing tensions between fundamentalists and the Starfleet crew.

Name: "The Homecoming"
Summary: Kira rescues a Bajoran Resistance hero from a Cardassian labor camp; an extremist group calls for all non-Bajorans to leave Bajor.

Name: "The Circle"
Summary: Sisko and Odo work to reveal the real force behind the Circle's coup.

Name: "The Siege"
Summary: Sisko tries to prevent the Circle from taking the station; Kira and Dax take proof that the Cardassians are the real force that is arming the Circle to the Bajoran government.

Name: "Invasive Procedures"
Summary: A desperate Trill tries to steal the Dax symbiont.

Name: "Cardassians"
Writer(s): Gene Wolande, John Wright, James Crocker
Summary: Garak and Doctor Bashir investigate abandoned Cardassian war orphans on Bajor.

Name: "Melora"
Writer(s): Evan Carlos Somers, Steven Baum, Michael Piller, James Crocker
Summary: Doctor Bashir ends up falling in love with a new officer when he develops a way for her to function in a high gravity environment. Meanwhile, Quark receives a death threat from one of his former associates.

Name: "Rules of Acquisition"
Writer(s): Hilary J. Bader, Ira Steven Behr
Summary: Grand Nagus Zek assigns Quark to initiate negotiations with a planet in the Gamma Quadrant, but Quark's new associate is not what he seems.

Name: "Necessary Evil"
Summary: An attempt on Quark's life re-opens a five-year-old murder investigation.

Name: "Second Sight"
Writer(s): Mark Gehred-O'Connell, Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Sisko falls in love with a woman visiting the station, but she is not what she appears to be.

Name: "Sanctuary"
Writer(s): Gabe Essoe, Kelley Miles, Frederick Rappaport
Summary: A group of refugees come through the wormhole in search of Kentanna, their fabled homeworld.

Name: "Rivals"
Writer(s): Jim Trombetta, Michael Piller, Joe Menosky
Summary: Quark feels threatened when a con artist arrives on the station and opens up a competing bar. Meanwhile, Chief O'Brien is determined to beat Doctor Bashir at racquetball.

Name: "The Alternate"
Summary: The Bajoran scientist who used to be Odo's teacher arrives with evidence of others of Odo's kind.

Name: "Armageddon Game"
Summary: O'Brien and Bashir help to rid two races of their biological weapons, however both governments want to ensure no technical knowledge of the weapons can survive.

Name: "Whispers"
Summary: Upon returning from a mission to the Parada system, O'Brien begins to notice the crew acting strangely around him and suspects there may be some unknown influence at work.

Name: "Paradise"
Writer(s): Jim Trombetta, James Crocker, Jeff King, Richard Manning, Hans Beimler
Summary: Sisko and O'Brien are trapped on a world with no advanced technology, and the Human colonists living there are determined to keep it that way.

Name: "Shadowplay"
Summary: At a colony in the Gamma Quadrant, Dax and Odo investigate the mysterious disappearance of several colonists.

Name: "Playing God"
Summary: While hosting her first Trill initiate Dax discovers a tiny, expanding protouniverse that threatens to destroy the Bajoran system.

Name: "Profit and Loss"
Summary: Quark is reunited with his lost Cardassian love, but he learns that she is a member of the Cardassian underground.

Name: "Blood Oath"
Summary: Three old Klingon warriors reunite on Deep Space 9, seeking Curzon Dax, with whom they entered into a blood oath to one day exact revenge on an enemy for killing the warriors' firstborn sons. Finding Jadzia as worthy a warrior as they felt Curzon to be, she joins the Klingons in completing their vendetta.

Name: "The Maquis, Part I"
Writer(s): Rick Berman, Michael Piller, Jeri Taylor, James Crocker
Summary: When a Cardassian freighter explodes at Deep Space 9, the Cardassians blame Federation colonists in the new Demilitarized Zone.

Name: "The Maquis, Part II"
Writer(s): Rick Berman, Michael Piller, Jeri Taylor, Ira Steven Behr
Summary: Sisko tries to rescue Gul Dukat, stop the Maquis terrorists, and prevent a new war with the Cardassians.

Name: "The Wire"
Summary: Bashir tries to help when Garak suffers painful headaches from an implant in his brain.

Name: "Crossover"
Summary: An accident inside the wormhole sends Kira and Bashir into the "mirror universe", where Klingons, Cardassians, and Bajorans rule over their Human slaves.

Name: "The Collaborator"
Writer(s): Gary Holland, Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Kira's lover is accused of collaborating with the Cardassians during the Occupation.

Name: "Tribunal"
Summary: When Cardassians arrest Miles O'Brien for working with the Maquis, he's put on a Cardassian trial, where the verdict is known before the trial begins: guilty.

Name: "The Jem'Hadar"
Summary: On a camping trip in the Gamma Quadrant, Sisko, Jake, Nog, and Quark encounter the ruthless soldiers of the Dominion, the Jem'Hadar.

Name: "The Search, Part I"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: Sisko takes an untested Starfleet warship into the Gamma Quadrant in an attempt to find the Founders of the Dominion.

Name: "The Search, Part II"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: On his homeworld, Odo learns about his people while back on the station, Sisko discovers that the price the Federation is willing to pay for peace with the Dominion may be too high.

Name: "The House of Quark"
Summary: After Quark lies about killing a Klingon in his bar, the dead man's widow abducts Quark to the Klingon homeworld to marry him.

Name: "Equilibrium"
Summary: Jadzia Dax is plagued by disturbing hallucinations that allude to the dark past of the Dax symbiont.

Name: "Second Skin"
Summary: Kira is kidnapped by the Cardassians, who try to convince her that she is really one of them.

Name: "The Abandoned"
Writer(s): D. Thomas Maio and Steve Warnek
Summary: Quark finds an abandoned Jem'Hadar child, and Odo is the only person who can control him.

Name: "Civil Defense"
Summary: Sisko, Jake, and O'Brien accidentally trigger an old Cardassian security system that believes the Occupation is still going on and the station has been taken in a Bajoran workers' rebellion.

Name: "Meridian"
Writer(s): Hilary J. Bader, Evan Carlos Somers, Mark Gehred-O'Connell
Summary: Jadzia falls in love with a scientist on a planet whose inhabitants shift between this universe and a plane of pure energy, re-emerging every sixty years. Back on DS9, Quark tries to obtain a holo-image of Major Kira for an erotic holosuite program for a wealthy patron.

Name: "Defiant"
Summary: When Commander William T. Riker from the Enterprise-D arrives on Deep Space 9, he takes a liking to Kira, who gives him a tour of the Defiant. But Riker is revealed to be not who he claims to be when he attacks Kira and steals the Defiant.

Name: "Fascination"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, James Crocker, Philip LaZebnik
Summary: Ambassador Lwaxana Troi visits the station to attend the Bajoran Gratitude Festival, resulting in an outbreak of passion throughout the station as people admit their secret feelings for others.

Name: "Past Tense, Part I"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Trapped three hundred years in the past, Sisko, Bashir, and Dax find themselves confronting one of the darkest hours in Earth's history…

Name: "Past Tense, Part II"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe, René Echevarria
Summary: With history itself at stake, Sisko must risk all to see that the Bell Riots reach their inevitable conclusion, even if it means sacrificing his life…

Name: "Life Support"
Writer(s): Christian Ford, Roger Soffer, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: After a serious accident, Bashir struggles to save the life of Vedek Bareil while Kai Winn concludes a peace treaty with Cardassia. Jake and Nog reluctantly explore the differences between Federation and Ferengi cultures.

Name: "Heart of Stone"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Searching for a Maquis raider on an unstable moon, Kira is trapped in an expanding crystal formation that threatens to engulf her if Odo cannot set her free. Meanwhile, Nog attempts to persuade a skeptical Commander Benjamin Sisko to write him a letter of recommendation to join Starfleet Academy.

Name: "Destiny"
Writer(s): David S. Cohen, Martin A. Winer
Summary: An ancient Bajoran prophecy of doom complicates the first joint Bajoran, Cardassian, and Federation science mission: an attempt to establish a permanent communications link through the wormhole.

Name: "Prophet Motive"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: When Grand Nagus Zek becomes a philanthropist and rewrites the Rules of Acquisition, Quark worries that he may have gone insane; Bashir is nominated for a prestigious medical award.

Name: "Visionary"
Summary: After receiving a minor dose of radiation poisoning, O'Brien inexplicably begins experiencing a series of jumps into the near future. Meanwhile, a Romulan delegation arrives on the station, expecting an intelligence report on the Dominion.

Name: "Distant Voices"
Writer(s): Joe Menosky, Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: After an alien assault leaves Bashir unconscious, he is trapped inside his mind.

Name: "Through the Looking Glass"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: In the "mirror universe," Sisko must persuade the alternate version of his dead wife to join the Terran Rebels, or he will watch her die a second time.

Name: "Improbable Cause"
Writer(s): Robert Lederman, David R. Long, René Echevarria
Summary: Odo begins an investigation after a bomb destroys Garak's tailor shop.

Name: "The Die is Cast"
Summary: The Cardassian–Romulan fleet enters the Gamma Quadrant; Sisko goes against Starfleet orders to rescue Odo.

Name: "Explorers"
Summary: Sisko builds a replica of an eight hundred-year-old Bajoran spaceship, and tries to use it to prove that Bajoran explorers could have made it to Cardassia without developing warp drive.

Name: "Family Business"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Quark returns home when his mother violates Ferengi law by earning profit.

Name: "Shakaar"
Summary: Kira's old Resistance leader's refusal to return some farming equipment to the Bajoran government nearly starts a civil war.

Name: "Facets"
Summary: Jadzia Dax performs the Trill zhian'tara ritual, which allows her to meet previous Dax hosts, while Nog applies to Starfleet.

Name: "The Adversary"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: A Federation ambassador brings newly-promoted Captain Sisko orders to take the Defiant on a patrol of the Tzenkethi border, where a destabilizing coup has just taken place, but everything is not as it seems.

Name: "The Way of the Warrior"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: When a Klingon fleet under General Martok arrives at the station ostensibly to protect the Alpha Quadrant from the Dominion, Sisko recruits Lieutenant Commander Worf to discover the Klingons' true intentions.

Name: "The Visitor"
Summary: After an accident in the engine room of the Defiant apparently claims the life of Benjamin Sisko, Jake lives out his life in an endless quest to locate his father.

Name: "Hippocratic Oath"
Summary: Bashir tries to help members of a Jem'Hadar unit free themselves of their addiction to the drug the Founders use to control them. Meanwhile, Worf tries to adjust to life aboard DS9.

Name: "Indiscretion"
Writer(s): Toni Marberry, Jack Treviño, Nicholas Corea
Summary: Kira and Dukat search for the six-year-old crash site of a Cardassian freighter that was carrying Bajoran prisoners. Also, Sisko deals with Kasidy moving onto the station, a new development in their relationship.

Name: "Rejoined"
Summary: Dax is reunited with the Kahn symbiont, a wife of one of her previous hosts, and must decide whether or not to ignore Trill taboo and continue their relationship.

Name: "Starship Down"
Writer(s): David Alan Mack, John J. Ordover
Summary: Sisko and the Defiant crew defend a Karemma ship when it is attacked by the Jem'Hadar. Meanwhile, Quark and the Karemma trade minister argue about the value of dishonesty in trading before having to work together to disarm a Jem'Hadar torpedo.

Name: "Little Green Men"
Writer(s): Toni Marberry, Jack Treviño, Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: A malfunction on Quark's new ship causes Quark, Rom, and Nog to crash in the year 1947 in Roswell, New Mexico.

Name: "The Sword of Kahless"
Summary: Klingon Dahar Master Kor, Jadzia Dax, and Worf search for the fabled Sword of Kahless on a remote planet in the Gamma Quadrant.

Name: "Our Man Bashir"
Summary: A transporter accident replaces the characters in Bashir's secret agent holosuite program with the physical forms of the station's senior staff.

Name: "Homefront"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Sisko is recalled to San Francisco after a terrorist bombing reveals that Changelings have reached Earth.

Name: "Paradise Lost"
Writer(s): Ronald D. Moore, Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: While Starfleet tightens security measures on Earth, Sisko and Odo discover that Admiral Leyton is deviously plotting to take over the planet.

Name: "Crossfire"
Summary: Odo must face his feelings for Kira when she falls in love with First Minister Shakaar, her former Resistance leader.

Name: "Return to Grace"
Summary: Kira and Gul Dukat chase the Klingon Bird-of-Prey that destroyed a Cardassian outpost where Cardassian and Bajoran representatives were holding a conference.

Name: "Sons of Mogh"
Summary: Worf's brother Kurn arrives on the station, and asks Worf to kill him. Meanwhile, Klingon ships are detected outside Bajoran space.

Name: "Bar Association"
Writer(s): Barbara J. Lee, Jenifer A. Lee, Robert Hewitt Wolfe, Ira Steven Behr
Summary: Quark's employees, led by Rom, form a union against Quark's unfair labor practices and promptly go on strike.

Name: "Accession"
Summary: A three-hundred-year-old Bajoran ship comes through the wormhole, and its passenger claims that he is the Emissary of the Prophets.

Name: "Rules of Engagement"
Writer(s): David Weddle, Bradley Thompson, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: The Klingons try to extradite Worf after he accidentally destroys a transport full of Klingon civilians.

Name: "Hard Time"
Writer(s): Daniel Keys Moran, Lynn Barker, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Convicted of espionage, Miles O'Brien is given the memories of twenty years in prison in a matter of hours. Returning to Deep Space 9, O'Brien finds he cannot shrug the memory of his awful experience or rid himself of the guilt he feels over the death of his cellmate.

Name: "Shattered Mirror"
Summary: Professor Jennifer Sisko uses Jake to lure Sisko to the "mirror universe" to help the rebels build another starship Defiant.

Name: "The Muse"
Summary: A mysterious woman helps Jake write a novel; Lwaxana Troi, pregnant with a son, asks Odo to help her escape her husband.

Name: "For the Cause"
Summary: Sisko suspects that Kasidy Yates may be a Maquis smuggler; Garak takes an interest in Ziyal.

Name: "To the Death"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Following a hit and run attack on Deep Space 9 by a band of rogue Jem'Hadar, Sisko and his crew are joined by the Dominion on a mission to locate the rebels, who have discovered another Iconian Gateway.

Name: "The Quickening"
Summary: Dr. Bashir works to rid a planet of a plague that was sent by the Dominion as punishment for resistance.

Name: "Body Parts"
Writer(s): Louis P. DeSantis, Robert J. Bolivar, Hans Beimler
Summary: When Quark learns that he is dying, he auctions his vacuum-desiccated body to raise capital. Meanwhile, an accident on a mission prompts Dr. Bashir to transfer Keiko's baby into Major Kira.

Name: "Broken Link"
Writer(s): George A. Brozak, Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Odo is plagued by an unknown ailment that threatens to kill him. Meanwhile, the Federation and the Klingon Empire move closer to war.

Name: "Apocalypse Rising"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Sisko leads a commando team into Klingon headquarters in an attempt to expose the Changeling impersonating Gowron.

Name: "The Ship"
Writer(s): Pam Wigginton, Rick Cason, Hans Beimler
Summary: Sisko fights to keep the wreckage of a crashed Jem'Hadar fighter.

Name: "Looking for par'Mach in All the Wrong Places"
Summary: Worf helps Quark woo Grilka, his Klingon ex-wife.

Name: "Nor the Battle to the Strong"
Summary: After diverting to the Federation hospital on Ajilon Prime looking for an interesting story, Jake believes himself to be a coward when repeated Klingon attacks awaken him to the reality of war and force him to abandon Dr. Bashir and run for cover.

Name: "The Assignment"
Writer(s): David R. Long, Robert Lederman, David Weddle, Bradley Thompson
Summary: After returning from the Fire Caves on Bajor, Keiko's body is controlled by an alien lifeform that forces her husband O'Brien to do its bidding or else face the death of his wife.

Name: "Trials and Tribble-ations"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Hans Beimler, Robert Hewitt Wolfe, Ronald D. Moore, René Echevarria
Summary: When Temporal Investigations arrives on Deep Space 9, Sisko recounts how he and the crew of the Defiant traveled back in time to the 23rd century to prevent the assassination of Captain James T. Kirk during the original Enterprise's mission to Space Station K-7.

Name: "Let He Who Is Without Sin..."
Writer(s): Robert Hewitt Wolfe, Ira Steven Behr
Summary: While Worf, Dax, Bashir, Leeta, and Quark vacation on Risa, Worf decides to join a radical fundamentalist group determined to start a political revolution on the planet.

Name: "Things Past"
Summary: Sisko, Odo, Dax, and Garak are trapped seven years in the past on Terok Nor, but everyone else thinks they're condemned Bajorans, and only Odo's memory can save them.

Name: "The Ascent"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Trapped on an inhospitable world, Quark and Odo must work together to survive. Meanwhile, Nog returns to the station from Starfleet Academy.

Name: "Rapture"
Summary: On the eve of Bajor's entry into the Federation, Sisko locates the ruins of the ancient lost city of B'hala on Bajor. As the visions that are guiding him prove potentially fatal, Sisko must choose between faith and his life.

Name: "The Darkness and the Light"
Summary: A hidden enemy systematically murders Kira's old Resistance comrades.

Name: "The Begotten"
Summary: Odo receives a sick infant Changeling from Quark and tries to teach it to shapeshift without resorting to the invasive techniques used by his old mentor, Doctor Mora. Meanwhile, Major Kira gives birth to the O'Briens' baby.

Name: "For the Uniform"
Summary: Sisko obsessively pursues Maquis leader Michael Eddington.

Name: "In Purgatory's Shadow"
Writer(s): Robert Hewitt Wolfe, Ira Steven Behr
Summary: Garak and Worf investigate a message which suggests that Cardassian spymaster Enabran Tain is still alive. Upon their arrival, not only do they find Tain, but also General Martok... and someone they did not expect.

Name: "By Inferno's Light"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: The crew tries to defend the Alpha Quadrant from the invading Dominion fleet; Worf, Garak, and the other prisoners prepare to escape from the Dominion Internment Camp.

Name: "Doctor Bashir, I Presume"
Summary: Doctor Lewis Zimmerman arrives on Deep Space 9 to use Bashir as the model for his new Long-term Medical Hologram, but his plans could unveil a dark secret that Bashir has carried since childhood.

Name: "A Simple Investigation"
Summary: Odo falls for a mysterious woman who is targeted for murder.

Name: "Business as Usual"
Summary: Quark's cousin Gaila offers him a job as a weapons dealer.

Name: "Ties of Blood and Water"
Writer(s): Edmund Newton, Robbin L. Slocum, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Kira asks Tekeny Ghemor to come to Deep Space 9 to provide information about the Cardassian government and the revitalizing dissident movement; Gul Dukat arrives and demands Ghemor's extradition.

Name: "Ferengi Love Songs"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr and Hans Beimler
Summary: Quark discovers that his mother and Grand Nagus Zek have fallen in love with each other. Rom and Leeta's relationship hits a rocky patch.

Name: "Soldiers of the Empire"
Summary: After Worf becomes first officer of a Klingon Bird-of-Prey commanded by General Martok, he is caught between loyalty to his commander and loyalty to the crew.

Name: "Children of Time"
Writer(s): Gary Holland, Ethan H. Calk, René Echevarria
Summary: Investigating a planet surrounded by a powerful energy field, the crew of the Defiant discovers their own descendants, and learns that in two days they will crash two hundred years in the past.

Name: "Blaze of Glory"
Writer(s): Robert Hewitt Wolfe, Ira Steven Behr
Summary: To prevent a Maquis missile attack from reaching Cardassia, Sisko must force Starfleet traitor Eddington to lead him to the launch site.

Name: "Empok Nor"
Summary: Scavenging an abandoned Cardassian space station identical to DS9 for equipment, O'Brien's team discovers that the station may not be completely abandoned.

Name: "In the Cards"
Writer(s): Truly Barr Clark, Scott J. Neal, Ronald D. Moore
Summary: Jake and Nog get into trouble while trying to cheer up Sisko by acquiring a mint-condition 1951 Willie Mays rookie baseball card; the Dominion offers to sign a nonaggression pact with Bajor.

Name: "Call to Arms"
Writer(s): Ira Steven Behr, Robert Hewitt Wolfe
Summary: Sisko attempts to prevent more Dominion ships from entering the Alpha Quadrant by mining the wormhole; Gul Dukat responds by launching a massive assault fleet against the station.

Name: "A Time to Stand"
Summary: With the Dominion on-track to winning the war against the Federation, Sisko and his crew take a captured Jem'Hadar ship into enemy territory with a mission to cut off the Jem'Hadar's supply of ketracel-white in the Alpha Quadrant.

Name: "Rocks and Shoals"
Summary: Sisko's crew crash land their Jem'Hadar ship into the waters of an alien ocean on a world where a group of Jem'Hadar have also crash landed with only one vial of ketracel-white remaining. Meanwhile, on Terok Nor, Kira finds she cannot live with herself working side by side with the Dominion.

Name: "Sons and Daughters"
Summary: Alexander Rozhenko joins the crew of the Rotarran, much to the disappointment of Worf. On Terok Nor, Tora Ziyal returns to the station where Dukat intends to use her to get closer to Major Kira.

Name: "Behind the Lines"
